title: Common envelope for density and derivative
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$, and let $M\ge0$. There is a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable function $b:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every $m,z\in\mathbb R^I$ with $|m_i|\le M$ for all $i$, both the absolute value of the product Gaussian density at $(m,z)$ and the operator norm of its mean derivative at $(m,z)$ are at most $b(z)$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. If $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, there exists a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable $b:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ such that $|G_v(m,z)|\le b(z)$ and $\|A_v(m,z)\|\le b(z)$ for all $z$ and all $m$ with $|m_i|\le M$ for every $i$, with operator norm for the maximum norm.
